problems.title: Round table
problems.statement: {{n}} friends sit around a round table. Two seatings count as the same if one is a rotation of the other, so everyone has the same left and right neighbours. How many different seatings are there?

common_wrong.feedback: That counts seatings in a row. Around the table, each seating is counted {{n}} times, once for each rotation.
Dividing by 2 removes mirror images, but here only rotations count as the same.

solution.title: Seat everyone in a row
solution.explanation: Ignoring the table's shape, {{n}} people can be ordered in {{n}}! ways.

solution.title: Divide out the rotations
solution.explanation: Rotating everyone one seat gives the same seating, and there are {{n}} rotations, so each seating was counted {{n}} times.

problems.title: Bracelet of beads
problems.statement: {{n}} different beads are threaded onto a bracelet. Two bracelets are the same if one can be rotated or flipped over to match the other. How many different bracelets are there?

common_wrong.feedback: That removes rotations but not flips. Turning the bracelet over gives the same bracelet, so each one is still counted twice.
That counts beads in a row. Each bracelet is counted once for every rotation and flip: {{n}} × 2 times.

solution.title: Order the beads in a row
solution.explanation: {{n}} different beads in a row can be ordered in {{n}}! ways.

solution.title: Divide out rotations and flips
solution.explanation: Each bracelet appears once for each of its {{n}} rotations, on each of its 2 sides, so divide by 2 × {{n}}.
